title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
issues: The paper's primary focus is adversarial corruption (prompt injection, corpus poisoning) defense, not knowledge conflict. While contradiction detection via NLI is used, knowledge conflict is explicitly noted as not the focus.
contribution: Proposes ReliabilityRAG, a defense framework using Maximum Independent Set on a contradiction graph (built via NLI over per-document answers) plus a weighted sample-and-aggregate scheme leveraging document reliability/rank to provide provable robustness against retrieval corruption (prompt injection, corpus poisoning).

title: Bounding Hallucinations: Information-Theoretic Guarantees for RAG Systems via Merlin-Arthur Protocols
issues: Paper uses adversarial training as a training-time mechanism for grounding/calibration rather than studying adversarial attacks/security on RAG. Fit to 'adversarial_corruption' (which usually denotes external attacks/poisoning) is weak; fit to 'calibration_control' (groundedness, abstention, info-theoretic guarantees) is strong.
contribution: Adapts the Merlin-Arthur interactive-proof protocol to RAG, training a generator with helpful and adversarial context maskers to induce grounded answers and abstention, and provides information-theoretic lower bounds (Explained Information Fraction) on context-answer mutual information.

title: MTRAG-UN: A Benchmark for Open Challenges in Multi-Turn RAG Conversations
issues: Paper is primarily an evaluation benchmark; relevance to uncertainty/calibration is indirect (handling unanswerable/underspecified via IDK / clarification). Not really OOD.
contribution: Introduces MTRAG-UN, a 666-task multi-turn RAG benchmark across 6 domains testing unanswerable, underspecified, non-standalone questions and clarification responses, showing frontier models struggle with abstention and clarification.

title: NeuroGenPoisoning: Neuron-Guided Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLM via Genetic Optimization of External Knowledge
issues: Paper is primarily an adversarial RAG poisoning attack. It addresses knowledge conflict only as an exploitation target (overriding parametric memory), not as a faithfulness/conflict-resolution study. Fits adversarial_corruption better than knowledge_conflict.
contribution: Proposes NeuroGenPoisoning, a neuron-attribution-guided genetic optimization attack that crafts poisoned external passages for RAG, activating 'Poison-Responsive Neurons' to override an LLM's parametric memory at scale.

title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
issues: This is a survey, not itself an adversarial corruption method. Better placed under survey_related.
contribution: A survey and benchmark (TRC Bench) of RAG trustworthiness across six dimensions—factuality, robustness, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy—reviewing attacks/defenses and evaluating 19 LLMs.
